reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes joining the Forsage earning system, directs viewers to inspect another account's earnings and team structure, and urges them to contact him to start. The demonstrated account page includes an upline signup prompt, partner/team fields, and a displayed profit figure, supporting a recruitment-dependent earning pitch rather than a neutral technical demonstration.

citations.quote: if you wants to start fosx then contact me fast
what is his earnings if he is a team size

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker’s stated purpose is to let viewers check whether someone’s income claim is true, not to ask them to take that claim on faith. He says viewers can see “how much income he has if he is telling the truth or not” and explains that they can inspect another person’s ID without that person’s password. That verification focus matters: teaching viewers to test an earnings claim is a different message from promising them the same earnings. The closing invitation to contact him if they want to start does introduce promotion, but it does not erase the video’s concrete instruction to check claims independently.

citations.quote: you can check how much income he has if he is telling the truth or not
you don't need a password to open the id of a person
if you wants to start fosx then contact me fast

rebuttal.rebuttal: The invitation to contact the speaker is real, but the prosecution’s reading leaves out his stated reason for showing the earnings page: checking “if he is telling the truth or not.” Nor does mentioning earnings alongside team size establish that the earnings came from recruiting that team. The displayed preview is evidence of what a viewer can inspect, not proof that the speaker promises the displayed result to anyone who joins.

citations.quote: if he is telling the truth or not
when that person joined how much is his earning as well as the team size

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The verification framing does not make this an investigation or warning. The speaker gives no criticism of the system; after walking through its earnings and team information, he asks viewers who want to start to contact him quickly. The account preview also places a signup prompt tied to an upline beside the profit and team fields. Taken together, those details support a recruitment pitch, even without an explicit guaranteed return.

opening.argument: The video is principally a walkthrough of an account-preview function. Its title promises to show how to check a person’s income, and the speaker gives sequential instructions for opening the site, signing in, and entering the ID or wallet ID of the person being checked. The demonstrated screen calls itself an “Account preview” and offers an ID or BUSD-wallet lookup. These are specific operating instructions a viewer could follow to examine an account. The brief closing invitation to contact the speaker should be weighed against that sustained demonstration, rather than treated as the purpose of every preceding step.

citations.quote: How to check income of any person in forsage platform
you will have to enter the ID & wallet ID of the person for whom you want the income
if you wants to start fosx then contact me fast

rebuttal.rebuttal: An interface can contain a signup button and team fields while a video about that interface remains instructional. The speaker specifically tells viewers to use preview to check when a person joined, their earnings, and team size. The prosecution identifies features of the page, but its opening does not show the speaker explaining how to recruit a team or claiming that signup produces the displayed profit.

citations.quote: click on preview you can check in it , when that person joined how much is his earning as well as the team size

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not isolated from promotion. The speaker moves from showing earnings and team size to inviting viewers to contact him to start. The preview page itself pairs a profit figure with partner and team fields and an upline signup prompt. A step-by-step format does not neutralize the invitation to join a system presented through earnings and recruitment-related features.

citations.quote: what is his earnings if he is a team size
if you wants to start fosx then contact me fast

opening.argument: Even allowing that the speaker offers help to people interested in starting, the evidence shows a contact invitation, not an articulated scheme for extracting money. He instructs viewers to look up an ID or wallet ID to inspect another account, and the preview displays earnings alongside account fields. The sampled program view also shows a zero-BUSD figure for a displayed program and zero partner and team counts. None of that establishes a required payment, a guaranteed return, or that the displayed profit was earned by recruiting others. Judge the invitation actually made, not a financial mechanism inferred from the mere presence of team-related fields.

citations.quote: if you wants to start fosx then contact me fast
you will have to enter the ID & wallet ID of the person for whom you want the income

rebuttal.rebuttal: The upline signup prompt is a significant interface detail, but it does not by itself show what the speaker would ask a viewer to pay or how a participant’s earnings are calculated. Likewise, his reference to team size identifies information available in a preview; it is not an explanation of commissions. The prosecution’s opening establishes promotional context, but it asks the judge to infer the alleged earning mechanism from adjacent fields.

citations.quote: how much is his earning as well as the team size

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A pitch need not spell out payment terms or promise guaranteed returns to promote recruitment-dependent earning. Here the speaker invites viewers to contact him to start immediately after explaining how to inspect earnings and team size. The account he demonstrates displays profit, partner and team fields, and “Sign up with this upline.” Those features supply the context missing from the defense’s account of the invitation.
